ocr.notes: Most text readable but with errors in names and numbers ('Hartgrave' as printed; '$2%' for '$25', 'Swand's' for 'Wand's'); last paragraph partly garbled.

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reported that friends of the gravely ill Tom Allen said he was being robbed, and that his daughter would ask the probate court to appoint a conservator over his property.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Sunday Morning, April 5, 1903, page 16. The paper spells the nurse's name 'Hartgrave'.

facts.fact: Allen's friends planned to apply to the probate court on Monday, April 6, 1903 for a conservator, saying 'quasi strangers' were taking advantage of his mental condition to get his property; his daughter Mrs. Mary Taylor of 3427 Clark Avenue was to make the affidavit
Allen was proprietor of the Champion's Rest, a saloon and dance hall at 619 Market Street
places: Champion's Rest, 619 Market Street, St. Louis

facts.fact: Robert Lyons, Allen's bartender for sixteen years and now proprietor of his own place at 732 South Seventh Street, said Mrs. Tillie Hartgrave, Allen's housekeeper, gave Gillespie a bill of sale for the saloon for $52.60
Lyons and Allen's daughter Mary Taylor went to the Baptist Hospital, where Allen had been for several days, and were refused permission to see him

Lyons said Mrs. Hartgrave had announced she would marry Allen as soon as she won the divorce she was suing for in the St. Louis circuit court; her maiden name was Sachs, her husband had been a salesman for Nelson Morris & Co. of Chicago, and she came from Kansas City

On April 3, 1903 Gillespie, an attorney and a notary came from Allen's room with a second bill of sale bearing Allen's 'mark', under which Gillespie would pay the hospital $25 a week for Allen's care if the Champion's Rest earned that much above expenses

It was rumored that others were trying to sell Allen's horse and buggy at Wand's livery stable, that his safety deposit box had been opened and $500 taken, and that a gold watch and chain given him by admirers and the deeds to his property were missing

notes: Index facts without ids also cover the deposit box and the horse.
